A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-D are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Sections 4-5 report original simulations and an NBA data analysis. Appendix B includes original hyperparameter sensitivity results and additional empirical findings.

after.justification: Sections 4-5 and Appendix B retain the work's original simulations, NBA analysis, and hyperparameter sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The spectral estimator, adaptive group penalty, optional refitting, change-detection objective, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. The new workflow diagram illustrates the existing procedure; naming the implementation package does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same two ranking-group simulation settings, two structural-change scenarios, and NBA regular seasons from 2014-2015 through 2018-2019. Applications mentioned in the new independence discussion are cited examples, not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GRC and KRC, Table 2 retains the naive change-detection baseline, and Appendix B.4 retains the GRC comparison for NBA grouping. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The sample configurations, metrics, bandwidths, discretization, EBIC selection, ten-fold cross-validation, and NBA candidate change points remain unchanged in Sections 4-5 and Appendix B. The sparsegl statement newly documents software rather than revising an experimental setting.

E4.justification: The refit comparison, hyperparameter sensitivity analyses in Appendix B.3, and supplementary NBA analysis in B.4 are retained. The new independence discussion adds no robustness experiment or dependence analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report 500 repetitions for the main simulations and 50 repetitions per hyperparameter combination. Neither introduces additional seed information, empirical uncertainty estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4, and 5 retain identical numerical entries. For example, setting 2 with n=50 and Mh=10 retains refit Kendall tau 0.9683 and MSE 0.0250. The NBA change points, groupings, and strength findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and Appendix C proofs are unchanged after matching numbering. Theorem 3.10 becomes 3.9 and Corollary 3.11 becomes 3.10. New Appendix D.1 discusses independence already assumed in Section 2.1 without modifying the formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about dynamic grouping, structural-change detection, consistency, estimator uncertainty, interpretability, and accuracy. No main contribution is added, removed, or substantively strengthened.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.1 argues that independent pairwise comparisons are a practical modeling simplification, citing sports, recommendation, and RLHF applications. This adds substantive justification of applicability. Existing smoothness, optimality, and empirical interpretations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a first-page code-repository link and identifies the R package sparsegl in Section 4.1. These provide additional access and implementation information; the previously documented hardware, hyperparameters, and experimental configurations are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Liang et al. (2024), Lu et al. (2025), Maystre et al. (2019), Xiong et al. (2024), Zhong et al. (2024), and Zhu et al. (2023). These expand software and independence-assumption context without redefining the central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, adopts the clearer term 'group consistency,' and moves v1 Remark 3.7 to Remark 2.1. It adds an independence subsection to Appendix D while retaining the overall section organization and most wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1, a workflow schematic showing pairwise observations, grouping, and dynamic programming. Existing Figures 1-5 become Figures 2-6, with adjusted placement and pagination. The existing empirical graphics and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The workflow diagram improves explanation, while the code-access link and sparsegl disclosure provide more useful reproduction guidance. Appendix D.1 contextualizes the existing independence assumption, although it adds no validation on the study data. These are limited quality gains; the method, empirical evidence, and proofs remain unchanged.
